families.name: CANCELLATION_COMPILE
families.coverage: Pre-cancelled InstanceCreator compilation is rejected with the original cancellation token before provider entry.

families.name: CANCELLATION_EXECUTION
families.coverage: Controlled providers produce one row, execution is cancelled, and the producer is released and observed to exit under an explicit budget.

families.name: ZERO_PROGRESS
families.coverage: Binary EOF zero-length elements and condition repeats prove ISE0009 progress and 10,000-iteration bounds through generated interpreters.

families.name: CLEANUP_TIMEOUT_CLASSIFICATION
families.coverage: Chunk consumers distinguish partial-work cleanup from finite success; harness budget expiry is an assertion failure carrying HARNESS_TIMEOUT.

contract.verificationResult: 48/48 frozen cases verified before the authoritative replay and again after it; no frozen expectation was replaced.

initialObservations.finding: The first compiled fixture replay exposed three harness/oracle issues: producer completion signaling and the zero-progress versus iteration-limit detail.
The producer completion assertion was isolated; the remaining failures were zero-progress detail classification.
The same two iteration-limit cases remained visible and were not counted as diagnostic passes.
The explicit iteration-limit oracle was corrected against the generated ParseException detail.
The calibrated fixture passed all cases; the source and product behavior were unchanged.
The frozen permanent matrix passed unchanged after contract freeze.

repairAttempts.note: All failures were retained and corrected in the test harness/oracle; no production code was changed.
Two green replays were retained, with r6 serving as the authoritative focused result.

focusedReplay.coverage: All 48 frozen identifiers execute through the real compilation, execution, generated-interpreter and chunk-pipeline paths.

harnessContract.budget: Each asynchronous scenario uses WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2)); synchronous generated interpretation is executed on a task with the same budget.
harnessContract.timeoutClassification: Budget expiry calls Assert.Fail with a HARNESS_TIMEOUT message and is not caught as a diagnostic success.
harnessContract.minimizedReproduction: The controlled provider emits one BasicEntity row and then waits on an owned release event; the zero-progress reproduction uses a zero-byte element or a 10,001-byte bounded repeat.
harnessContract.resourceBoundary: No process environment, user cache, external provider or unbounded input is used.

obligations.REC-133-O01: The CC family cancels compilation before provider entry, the EX family cancels execution after a produced row, and the ZP family proves generated ISE0009 progress and iteration-limit paths.
obligations.REC-133-O02: The fixture uses explicit two-second WaitAsync budgets and a controllable provider/session. It does not invent a Musoq runtime limit.
obligations.REC-133-O03: The EX family observes a producer started after partial work and releases it in the cleanup path; CL-01 through CL-08 assert cancellation-aware consumer disposal and producer exit while CL-09 through CL-12 assert finite success.
obligations.REC-133-O04: Harness timeouts are explicit assertion failures with HARNESS_TIMEOUT text. The minimized controlled provider and zero-progress reproductions are retained in the permanent fixture and failed exploratory TRXs remain preserved.
obligations.acceptance: All 48 frozen cases passed, all bounded scenarios terminated through their contracted cancellation, cleanup or ISE0009 path, and no production finding required repair.
